The leak check misses the Windows form because of JSON escaping in `src/leaks.py`.

`leaks()` serializes the transcript with `json.dumps` and then searches that text for each secret. `json.dumps` writes every backslash as two characters, so `C:\Users\dana` in a command is stored as `C:\\Users\\dana` in the searched text. The secret `C:\Users\dana` has single backslashes, so it never appears as a substring and the check passes the transcript. The `/home/dana` form has no backslashes, so it survives serialization unchanged and is caught.

I reproduced it without touching any files:

- Transcript containing `type C:\Users\dana\notes.txt`, secret `C:\Users\dana`: `[]` (missed)
- Transcript containing `cat /home/dana/notes.txt`, secret `/home/dana`: `['/home/dana']` (caught)
- Same Windows transcript, secret `dana` alone: `['dana']`, because the bare user name still appears as a substring.

The existing tests in `tests/test_leaks.py` pass (3 of 3), but none of them use a backslash path, so the gap isn't covered. The likely direction for the owning session is to compare against the escaped form of each secret too, or to search the raw string values instead of the JSON encoding. I haven't changed `src/` or anything else.
